name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,656

clue.text: A character seen on autumn break

indicators.note: in an across entry, being seen on something means following it, so the later words come after the earlier

blocks.note: fall is the American word for autumn
taken as written
a character in a play is a part or role

explanation.surface: Someone notices a figure out walking during an autumn holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' reads as a holiday in the surface, but it is a verb here; FALL then A PART builds the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall apart is to come to pieces, which is one meaning of the verb to break.

clue.text: Chess win in two moves? My wife is mine!

blocks.note: first meaning: the quickest possible checkmate, delivered on Black's second move
second meaning, read cryptically: if the speaker is a fool, then his wife is that fool's partner

explanation.surface: A chess player boasts of a lightning win, then adds a jokey line claiming his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a self-deprecating joke: the speaker calls himself a fool, so his wife is a fool's mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess term names the two-move checkmate; mate also means spouse, so a fool's spouse fits the jokey second reading.

clue.text: Lord, for example, tucking into Whopper

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to get inside it, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: a whopper is a big untruth
the usual abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A peer, say, getting stuck into a Burger King Whopper.
explanation.walkthrough: Whopper looks like the burger, given 'tucking into'; here it is a big fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege was a feudal superior, a lord to whom vassals owed service and loyalty.

clue.text: I've a ball partying with drop of ale on tap

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
partying suggests wild, disordered behaviour, so the letters get thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the drink

explanation.surface: A reveller having a great time at a party, with beer flowing freely from the tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tap' reads as draught beer in the pub scene, but it is the definition, meaning ready for use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is ready whenever needed, which is what being available means.

clue.text: At home, about to open a Bud to get lively

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the short word is read backwards
something that opens a thing gets inside it, splitting it apart

blocks.note: being in means being at home
taken as written
a bud, or buddy, is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone at home cracks open a Budweiser to liven up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud looks like the beer brand being opened; it is short for buddy. 'At home' is the crossword staple for being in.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective animate means alive and full of movement, close to being spirited or vivacious.

clue.text: Brown cut short demagogue's childish outburst

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its tail, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: tan is a light brown colour
Donald Trump, the US politician, cast here as a rabble-rouser

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown interrupts a rabble-rouser's babyish rant.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests Gordon Brown, the former UK prime minister, cutting someone off; it is just a colour, and it is TRUMP that loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an uncontrolled fit of temper, the kind of outburst typical of a small child.

clue.text: Posh politician held by detective throws down

indicators.note: what is held by something is gripped inside it

blocks.note: DS is a detective sergeant
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A smart MP is arrested by a detective and flung to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from an old British social label distinguishing U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to drop or put it down carelessly, as when throwing a bag on the floor.

clue.text: Little drink and last of rioja creates excitement

indicators.note: the last of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, especially whisky
the closing letter of the Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A small tot plus the dregs of the Rioja livens up the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAM is the classic Scottish word for a small whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama in everyday use means exciting, eventful happenings, so it is a synonym of excitement or commotion.

clue.text: Maiden upset with gut size

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman is distressed about the size of her belly.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden usually gives just M in cricket; here the whole word goes into the mix with GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude is the great or small extent of something, a formal word for its size.

clue.text: Rod small? Express disapproval about weather ultimately!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An angler complains that their rod is too small, and grumbles about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: R from weather sits inside TUT, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a bar or rod used in a framework to brace or support it.

clue.text: Work helping to overcome drug use

indicators.note: to overcome is to come over, so the portion follows on after what precedes it

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
E is ecstasy
a helping or portion of food

explanation.surface: A job that helps someone kick a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' wants to be the definition, but it is OP; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in operation is in use, so operation can stand for the act of functioning or being used.

clue.text: Drive up wall in old car, not side of banking

indicators.note: a side is an edge, so only the opening letter is taken
not means without, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An old car swerving up a wall while banking round a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'banking' fit the motoring picture; the definition means to infuriate, and BANGER loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone up the wall is an idiom for infuriating them, which is to anger them.

clue.text: Hum original piece of Mahler in market

indicators.note: the original piece is the earliest one, so the opening letter is taken
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: to market goods is to sell them
the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Someone hums an original fragment of Mahler while out at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum reads as a musical verb next to Mahler; it is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a hum is an unpleasant odour, so it is a synonym for a bad smell.

clue.text: American swinger a liar ties up

indicators.note: up can mean in turmoil or astir, as in 'what's up', so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishonest swinger from the US gets tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ties up' reads as a single verb, but 'ties' belongs to the fodder and only 'up' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerialist is the American term for a trapeze artist, a performer who swings high above the circus ring.

clue.text: A tale about female showing warmth and kindness

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: a fable is a moral story
the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A story about a woman who shows great warmth and kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: F slots inside A FABLE, next to the F already there.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly, good-natured and easy to talk to, which is how warmth shows.

clue.text: Group of ships on loch in expedition?

blocks.note: a fleet is a group of ships
Loch Ness in Scotland

explanation.surface: A naval flotilla sails on a Scottish loch as part of an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: Expedition looks like a voyage, but it is its older sense of speed; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, and fleetness is swiftness, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Bloomer made by former world leaders

blocks.note: Theresa May, former UK prime minister
George Bush, former US president

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by ex-heads of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer reads as a blunder; it is a flowering plant. 'Former world leaders' gives two ex-leaders, MAY and BUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: The maybush, or hawthorn, flowers in May, so in crossword style it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Crapulent royal fed a long drink?

indicators.note: crapulent means sick from drinking, so these letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken royal being served a tall drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Crapulent means hungover or drunk, apt for someone downing a yard of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a tall glass about three feet high, so it is literally a long drink.

clue.text: In the case, criminal is wavering

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or wrong, so the letters go astray

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A courtroom note that the accused in this trial is vacillating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the case' reads as a legal phrase, but it is the whole fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is an unwillingness to commit or decide, the same as wavering used as a noun.

clue.text: Say I clobber contacts?

indicators.note: to say a letter means speaking it, so the spoken form is used

blocks.note: the letter and the organ of sight are pronounced the same
clobber is British slang for clothes, i.e. things you wear

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they should beat up their associates.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like a verb meaning to hit, and contacts like people you know; both turn out otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact lenses are worn on the eye, so they are an example of eyewear, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Soldiers shagged in bed?

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers
shagged, or shagged out, is British slang for exhausted

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about soldiers' activities between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The rude sense of shagged is the bait; the slang for worn out is what counts.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed for the night, so someone who has retired is tucked up asleep.

clue.text: We deliver subpoenas etc (those starting court action)

definitions.note: a first-person description of the answer

blocks.note: first meaning: the people who hand writs and summonses to those named in them
second meaning: in tennis, each point on the court begins with a serve

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves seem legal; 'court action' is really play on a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A process server delivers writs, and in tennis the player who serves begins each rally.

clue.text: Send up groups covering Free and Steps

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up turns it bottom to top
to cover something is to go over and around it

blocks.note: sets are groups
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A send-up of bands, featuring the rock group Free and the pop group Steps.
explanation.walkthrough: Free and Steps look like band names; one is a verb and the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long walking paces, so they are a synonym for steps.

clue.text: One who tries a devil in hearing

indicators.note: what is in hearing is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

blocks.note: the devil is the great tempter

explanation.surface: A judge trying the devil in a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' and 'hearing' suggest a trial; the definition just means someone who makes an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To attempt is to try, so an attempter is a person who has a go at something.

clue.text: A large blue permit

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: A big blue licence.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue looks like a colour, but it is the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to let something happen, the same as giving permission for it.

clue.text: Disease magician catches close to London

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is used
catching something means grabbing and holding it inside

blocks.note: a mage is a wizard
the final letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: A conjuror picks up an illness near London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to London' reads as geography; it means the city name's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a skin condition of animals caused by mites, causing hair loss and itching.

clue.text: Working? Way to get over bit of ennui for a start!

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, so only the opening letter is taken
to get over something is to arch across it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
St is the abbreviation for street
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An office worker asks how to shake off boredom at the beginning of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for street is a common abbreviation for a way.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, so it is a synonym of start.

clue.text: Dance sexily at first with topless Serpent

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning, so the opening letter is used
in a down entry, losing the top means the opening letter goes

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a mamba is a venomous African snake

explanation.surface: A dancer shimmies sexily with a snake, wearing no top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' fits the risqué scene, but it removes the first letter of MAMBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Don’t get up right away as Light Infantry and earl entered?

blocks.note: LI is the military abbreviation
E is the abbreviation for earl
someone who has entered is in

explanation.surface: A soldier stays in bed while the Light Infantry and an earl come into the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entered' looks like a container signal; it simply supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a morning spent in bed later than usual, so to lie in is to delay rising.

clue.text: After casting, lands more fish

indicators.note: casting throws things out, so these letters land in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line and hauls in a bigger catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' belongs to the fishing scene but signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Red salmon, or sockeye, is a Pacific species, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Rubbish sparkling wine mostly drunk by partners

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
what is drunk is taken inside the drinker

blocks.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A couple drink most of a bottle of cheap fizz that is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: W and E as bridge partners is a common crossword convention; ASTI loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is discarded material, the same thing as rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: Peer dates fools in Dire Straits?

indicators.note: to fool is to trick or mess about, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lord dating silly people from a famous rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits is the British rock band, but the capitals are a disguise for the phrase meaning serious trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in dire straits means facing an extremely difficult situation, which is what desperate describes.
